0.0.n: 今から sets the present as the starting point for counting backward.

0.1.n: Marks the starting point, here the present.

0.2.n: 年 counts years; 前 later makes this a time in the past.

0.3.n: After a number, くらい makes the amount approximate.

0.4.n: After a time span, 前 places it that far in the past.

0.6.n: Describes 国 and also helps encode 1192 in this historical memory aid.

0.7.n: This subtitle chunk combines 国 with part of 作ろう; the usual を after 国 is omitted.

0.8.n: This is the final portion of 作ろう, the form of 作る used to suggest doing something together.

0.9.n: A place name used here as part of the shogunate’s name.

0.10.n: Names a government headed by a shogun, a military ruler.

1.0.n: A place name that also names this historical period.

1.1.n: Combines with 鎌倉 to name an era in Japanese history.

1.2.n: Marks the Kamakura period as what the sentence is about.

1.3.n: Gives the duration directly before くらい and 続きます; no extra particle is needed.

1.5.n: Polite nonpast form of 続く, used here to narrate a historical event.

2.0.n: A clan name; 氏 identifies a family or lineage.

2.1.n: Links the clan to its leader, トップ.

2.2.n: An English loanword used casually for the person at the head of an organization.

2.4.n: The family name in 源頼朝; the full name is conventionally read with の between family and given names.

2.5.n: The given name of the historical figure 源頼朝.

2.7.n: Identifies 源頼朝 as the person establishing headquarters.

2.8.n: A place name identifying where he establishes his base.

2.9.n: Marks the location where the headquarters is established.

2.10.n: Refers to the main base from which someone operates.

2.11.n: Marks 本拠地 as what he establishes.

2.12.n: Polite nonpast form of 構える; 本拠地を構える means to set up a main base.

3.0.n: Here, 今 refers to the point reached in the historical story, not the present day.

3.1.n: Sets the endpoint of the earlier situation; 今まで means up to this point.

3.2.n: The title of Japan’s monarch, rather than a personal name.

3.3.n: Identifies 天皇 as the person who held power.

3.4.n: 者 adds the sense of a person to 権力, political power.

3.5.n: This is the first part of でした, the polite past form of です.

3.6.n: Completes でした, placing the emperor’s position in the past.

3.7.n: Connects two clauses while contrasting the earlier and later power holders.

3.9.n: Points forward from this moment in the historical narrative.

3.10.n: Highlights the coming period in contrast with the earlier one.

3.11.n: Refers collectively to the warrior class, not necessarily one individual.

3.12.n: Identifies 武士 as the new holders of political power.

3.13.n: Refers to authority over government and society, rather than physical strength.

3.14.n: Marks 権力 as what the samurai possess.

3.15.n: Polite nonpast form of 持つ; here it describes possessing authority rather than physically carrying something.

0.lit: From now, about 830 years before: let’s build a good nation, Kamakura shogunate.
0.tip: いい国 is a number-based memory aid for 1192, the traditional founding date of the Kamakura shogunate.

1.lit: As for the Kamakura period, it lasts about 150 years.
1.tip: Japanese often narrates history with nonpast verbs like 続きます, even when English naturally uses past tense.

2.lit: The Minamoto clan’s leader, Minamoto no Yoritomo, establishes headquarters in Kamakura.
2.tip: に marks where the base is established, while を marks the base itself as what is established.

3.lit: Until now, the emperor was the person in power, but from now on, samurai hold power.
3.tip: 今まで and これから contrast time before and after this point in the story, not before and after today.
